color.$description: Layer 2 semantics. These are the only color tokens component code is allowed to name. Every value is a reference into Layer 1 and every name describes the job the color does, never what it looks like: repoint a primitive and this file still reads correctly. The values here are the DARK theme, which is the default and lives on :root. tokens/themes/light.json overrides this same set and nothing else.

surface.$description: Elevation on a dark UI is expressed by stepping this token, not by stacking shadows. sunken sits behind everything (the page, an inset field, a track well), base is the default plane, raised is a card or panel on it, overlay is a menu, popover or dialog above the whole thing. Four steps is the entire vocabulary; needing a fifth means something is nested too deep.

border.$description: Hairlines, always translucent so one value holds up over any surface step. subtle is the default and is nearly invisible by design: it should separate, not divide. strong is for a control that has to read as an editable boundary.

muted.$description: Secondary text: labels, metadata, timestamps. Still clears 4.5:1 on surface.base. It is muted, not disabled, and there is deliberately no third dimmer tier, because a third tier is where hierarchy turns into illegibility.

on-primary.$description: The label on a filled amber control. Resolves to a near-black, and that is correct: see palette.amber.contrast for why it can never be white. Identical in both themes, because primary.solid is identical in both themes.

primary.$description: The amber accent in its three jobs. For the one action in a view that matters most. A screen with three primary buttons has none.

text.$description: Amber as text or an icon rather than a fill: a link, an active nav item, a chord symbol. This is the token that has to flip between themes, because amber bright enough to read on near-black is far too light to read on near-white.

solid.$description: The teal counter-accent as a fill, for a second axis of meaning that would be ambiguous in amber. The intended first use is marking a capo transform as distinct from a key change.

track.$description: Identity colours for tracks, voices and pads. Assign them in order and let them repeat; nothing about track 1 makes it more important than track 4. Like the amber, they take a near-black label: at this lightness white lands near 2.5:1 and the label would be the thing that gives.

focus-ring.$description: Always visible, never removed. An outline may be replaced with a different visible treatment; it may not be replaced with nothing. This is the one place the accent appears without being the primary action, because the user put it there by pressing Tab.
